interpretation: The TensorFlow MLP does not learn a useful compatibility classifier from the current feature set.
The current features are only product type, canonical category and outfit role for input/candidate items.
Hard negatives are generated at item level, but the model cannot see item identity, image, color, style, title or embedding information.
Many negative examples can therefore share exactly the same product_type/role pattern as positive examples, making the supervised binary task weak or contradictory at feature level.
The earlier cooccurrence baseline remains the defendable MVP path because it is directly aligned with product_type recommendation instead of item-level binary classification.

The ranking metrics in this experimental training report are not directly comparable to the earlier leakage-filtered cooccurrence baseline report, whose valid/test recall_at_3 values were computed on product-type recommendation from real positive pairs.
recommended_next_steps: Do not copy models/outfit_v1 to models/outfit_active.
Present Outfit V1 as an experimental TensorFlow attempt that demonstrates evaluation discipline and non-promotion when metrics are weak.

If a stronger Outfit V2 is required, add more informative features: color harmony, image embeddings from Fashion V1/MobileNet, title/category text embeddings, style attributes or learned product embeddings.
Evaluate future models as ranking/recommendation systems against the cooccurrence baseline, not only as binary classifiers on synthetic negatives.
Keep the MVP service on the leakage-filtered cooccurrence baseline plus coded color/outfit rules.
